title: [Feature][DSA] Share O-projection buffers across DeepSeek layers
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR reduces resident OTP communication-buffer memory for DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 by sharing address-stable O-projection exchange scratch across sequential DSA layers. It reserves the shared buffers before KV-cache profiling and sizes them for the largest decode graph capacity, so profiling accounts for their resident memory without sizing them to the larger profiling-token budget. Empty DSA ranks now still enter OTP O-projection collectives during ragged DP decoding. Buffer reservation also initializes its pool defensively for standalone attention instances.

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No new user-facing option or API. The change affects internal OTP buffer allocation and KV-cache memory accounting when O-projection tensor parallelism is enabled.

## How was this patch tested?

- Added or updated unit coverage in `tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v1.py`, `tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v41.py`, `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_dspark.py`, and `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_context_wkv.py`.
- On the 108 `lhf_vllm` container, four focused OTP tests passed: 9 passed.
- The full `test_dsa_v1.py` run did not complete; it aborted during Triton compilation of `dspark_swa_indices.py` after earlier test failures. This is not counted as a passing run.
- `python -m py_compile` and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files. `bash format.sh ci` could not run because `pre-commit` is not installed in the container; Ruff is also unavailable.
- Multi-rank HCCL validation has not been run.
